newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai Telephone completes lines contract.
newsitem.headline: Thai Telephone completes lines contract.

text.p: Thai Telephone and Telecommunication Plc said on Wednesday it had installed 1.5 million provincial telephone lines in Thailand by a government-set September 30 deadline.
The deadline was set by the state-owned Telephone Organisation of Thailand (TOT). The project brings the total number of fixed lines in Thailand to 6.26 million.
Installation costs were 31,300 baht ($1,300) per line. The company has so far connected 853,300 users.
Company President Tongchat Hongladaromp told reporters that take-up was below expectations because of Thailand's reduced growth rate this year and other factors in some upcountry areas.
Chief Executive Officer Adisai Bodharamik said the firm had asked the TOT to reduce long distance provincial call charges by 33 percent to encourage connections.
It also planned to add public payphones to its network, and revenue sharing negotiations with TOT were underway.

He said TOT last month gave the go-ahead for the company to begin a cordless phone system, based on its existing fixed lines. TTNT said it plans to incorporate a wholly owned subsidiary to begin running the service in seven provinces within nine months.
